summary: HarborTech production surge: warm-start latency amplification and unordered streaming fragments (major incident)
description: Issue summary: During a customer-driven traffic surge and scheduled canary workload ramp (HarborTech), production requests experienced a sudden multi-minute warm-start latency amplification followed by a period of unordered streaming fragments (stream pieces arriving out of sequence or truncated). Impact: Customers reported increased completion latency (p95 for short-chat flows rose from ~120ms to ~2.3s) and intermittent transcript reordering for streamed responses. Two HarborTech endpoints observed duplicated partial chunks and out-of-order final tokens for ~22 minutes, triggering an enterprise escalation. Environment: production cluster serving us-east-1; affected pool: dedicated-dp-ht-02 (reserved capacity).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use HarborTech workload template (conversation payloads averaging 120 tokens, concurrency spike from 50 to 1,200 QPS) against dedicated pool dp-ht-02. 2) Trigger a cold-to-warm transition by spinning up new worker slices with kernel/quantization variant redwood-open-xxl-v1-quantized. 3) Observe request latencies during the first 10 minutes of scale-up and monitor streaming chunk ordering (chunk sequence IDs and chunk timestamps).
logs: Key logs: serving-runtime/worker-127.log: repeated KV-cache eviction events during startup (timestamps 2026-03-11T09:03:10Z - 09:09:31Z). Router traces show request multiplexing reassignments to warm workers with missing seq metadata (router/assign-4632.trace). Observability: p95 token latencies spike in dashboard shard 'dp-ht-02' corresponding to autoscale events; traces linked: https://observability.redwood.com/trace/HT-0311-1, https://observability.redwood.com/trace/HT-0311-2.

investigation_notes: Observation 1: Warm-worker startup sequences coincided with autoscale events at 09:02-09:25 UTC. Workers entered warm state but triggered repeated KV-cache eviction heuristics immediately after initialization.

Observation 2: Kernel selector telemetry shows flapping between fast-quantized kernels and compatibility fallback kernels for the same model during first 2-3 minutes after spin-up. The fallback path increases per-token CPU overhead and also delays sequence assembly in stream multiplexers.

Hypothesis: The quantized variant's startup path does not prepopulate required prefix KV entries, triggering eviction heuristics and causing repeated cache misses. Combined with routing reassignment, some stream fragments lost sequencing metadata, leading to reorder/truncation at the router/stream reassembly layer.

Evidence: Heap and KV metrics (serving-runtime/metrics) show KV-miss rate spike x18 during warm window. Router logs show 'missing-seq-metadata' events correlated with worker IDs that recently joined the pool. GitHub trace of kernel selector shows recent change in PR #1248 altered compatibility fallback threshold.

Temporary mitigations tested: 1) Pin to full-precision variant — success, reduces tail. 2) Increase KV cache soft limit on warm nodes — partial improvement. 3) Coordinate ingress routing to avoid reassigning in-flight streams during worker warmup — blocked by router code lacking warmup-tag awareness.
resolution_notes: Root cause: Interaction of a recent kernel-selection threshold change (PR #1248) with quantized model warm-start sequence. Newly started workers were allowed to serve before full prefix/KV priming completed; automatic KV-eviction heuristics then triggered repeated evictions leading to cache thrash and delayed token generation. Router reassignment of some in-flight streams to these partially warm workers resulted in missing sequence metadata and reordered/truncated streaming fragments.

Immediate fix: Rolled back dp-ht-02 to redwood-open-xxl-v1 (non-quantized) and increased KV cache soft limits on warm workers. Also disabled the new aggressive fallback threshold in kernel selector for the affected pool. This restored p95 latency and eliminated stream reorder incidents within 9 minutes.

Permanent fix planned: Platform Eng to publish a warmup contract for workers so router can annotate/avoid in-flight reassignment until worker reports 'primed' state. Also revert or refine PR #1248 to include a delayed-serve gating during KV priming. Add a unit/regression test for stream sequence metadata preservation across worker handoffs.
Customer remediation: Provided HarborTech with an incident summary, one day service credit for affected dedicated pool time window, and scheduled architecture review.
